cases.lesson: Seven of eleven early starters produced no trades because their configured live lookback could not satisfy strategy warmup. Reject candidates whose live window cannot reach their first valid decision.
Diversified passive capitulation was more stable than concentrated HYPE-only variants; apparent maker improvements remain hypotheses when queue position and partial fills are not modelled.
The durable momentum result came from the simple base. Smoothing, score gates, dynamic volatility, and diversified-selection branches were removed after failing their ablations.
A broad-rally overlay improved the recent run but was inspired by that same run and did not activate in older folds. Treat it as a forward-test hypothesis, not independent holdout evidence.
Early factor positives vanished after correcting mislabeled timeframes, start-labeled funding, and rank-buffer overflow. Verify timestamp semantics and capacity before scoring economics.
Leverage frequently converted acceptable unlevered paths into risk-halt breaches. Search signal and exit structure separately from exposure scaling.
Recent owner live evidence concentrated most losses in one symbol while aggregate win rate obscured it. Always inspect symbol, direction, and exit attribution before changing the whole strategy.
Candidates are comparable only when fees, funding, next-open execution, interval labels, and feature availability match between incumbent, candidate, and forward paths.

Live decide() sees a bounded window of completed bars; any backtest logic consuming more history than the declared warmup_bars is testing a strategy that cannot exist in production, and recomputing over full history turns replays quadratic. Declare the window, compute within it, carry long memory as incremental state.
